items.title: Section: What Form Depends Upon, What Mind Depends Upon — And the Six General Aspects at Last Complete

items.zh: 依止幾處，色蘊轉耶？依止幾處，名所攝四蘊轉耶？謂依止六，處色蘊轉。一、建立處，二、覆藏處，三、資具處，四、根處，五、根住處，六、有威德定所行處。依止七處，名所攝四蘊轉。一、樂欲，二、希望，三、境界，四、尋伺，五、正知，六、清淨方便，七、清淨。諸受用欲者，依止四處；住律儀者、精進行者，依止一處；已得近分定者，依止一處；安住根本定者，依止一處。如是七處，略有四位應知。復次，我當先說分別色蘊一一別義，然後分別名四蘊義。云何分別色蘊？嗢拕南曰：物、極微、生起、安立、與流、業、剎那、獨、所行、餘相雜最後。
items.en:
Depending on how many grounds does form aggregate occur? Depending on how many grounds do the four name-aggregates occur? Form aggregate occurs depending on six grounds: the ground of establishment, the ground of shelter, the ground of requisites, the ground of the faculties, the ground the faculties depend upon, and the ground of the meditative states of those with great spiritual power.
The four name-aggregates occur depending on seven grounds: desire, hope, the object, investigation-and-analysis, correct awareness, the expedient means to purity, and purity. Those who enjoy sensory pleasure depend on four grounds; those upholding discipline or practising diligently depend on one; those who have attained access concentration depend on one; those abiding in a fundamental absorption depend on one.
Next, I shall first explain form aggregate's own particular meanings one by one, and afterwards explain the meanings of the four aggregates. How is form aggregate to be analysed? A mnemonic verse states: kind, subtlest constituents, arising, establishment, and continuity and function, momentary cessation, distinct character, and what is operated upon, the remainder intermixing, and last of all —
Question: by how many things is the eye, within form aggregate, comprised?

items.title: Section: How Many "Things" Make an Eye? Three Ways of Counting, From One Up to Ten

items.zh: 問：色蘊中眼，幾物所攝？答：若據相攝，唯有一物。謂眼識所依清淨色。若據不相離攝，則有七物。謂即此眼及與身、地、色、香、味、觸。若皆據界攝，則有十物。即此七物界及水、火、風界。如眼耳、鼻、舌當知亦爾。此中差別者，謂耳、耳識所依清淨色，鼻、鼻識所依清淨色，舌、舌識所依清淨色。餘如前說。若身，當除眼等四。何以故？由遠離彼獨可得故。
items.en:
Question: by how many things is the eye, within form aggregate, comprised? Answer: by subsumption according to characteristic, only one thing — the pure matter eye-consciousness depends upon. By subsumption according to inseparability, seven things — this same eye, together with body, earth, colour, smell, taste, and touch. By subsumption according to seed, ten things — these same seven, together with the water, fire, and wind elements. As with the eye, so too should the ear, nose, and tongue be understood.
For the body, one should exclude the eye and the other three. Why? Because it can be obtained independently, apart from them.

items.zh: 此相者，謂身識所依清淨色。

items.title: Section: Why Sound Is Different — Present Only Sometimes, Yet Latent Everywhere

items.zh: 若於外色、香、味、觸彼所行相中，除一切根，餘一切如前應知。聲及聲界不恒有故，今當別說。若於是處有聲，當知此處復增其一。應知聲界，一切處增。復次，色等所緣境界，如本地分已廣分別。
items.en: For the external objects of colour, smell, taste, and touch, excluding all the faculties, the rest should be understood as before. Sound and the sound-element are not constantly present, and so must now be explained separately. Wherever sound is present, one should know that place gains one further member. One should know that the sound-element is added as one further member everywhere. Furthermore, the objects of colour and the rest have already been extensively analysed in the Stage of Mind.

items.title: Section: Twenty Tactile Sensations, All Provisional Names for the Four Elements' Shifting States

items.zh: 若觸處中所說造色滑乃至勇，當知即於大種分位假施設有。謂於大種清淨性，假立滑性。於大種堅實性，假立重性。於大種不清淨、不堅實性，假立澁性及輕性。於大種不清淨、慢緩性，假立軟性。由水與風和合生故，假立有冷。由闕任持不平等故，假立飢渴及弱力。由無所闕無不平等故，假立強力及飽。由不平等變異錯亂不平等故，假立病。由時分變異不平等故，假立老。由命根變異不平等故，假立死。由血有過患不平等故，假立癢。由惡飲食不平等故，假立悶絕。由地與水和合生故，假立黏。由往來勞倦不平等故，假立疲極。若遠離彼，由平等故，假立憩息。由除垢等離萎顇故，假立勇銳。如是一切，說諸大種總有六位。謂淨不淨位、堅不堅位、慢緩位、和合位、不平等位、平等位。如是六位，復開為八。若八、若六，平等平等。
items.en:
What is said of tactile derived matter — smoothness up through vigour — should be known as provisionally designated upon a particular state of the four elements. Upon the elements' own purity, smoothness is provisionally established. Upon their firmness, heaviness. Upon their impurity and lack of firmness, roughness and lightness. Upon their impure sluggishness, softness. Because water and wind combine, coldness is established. Because of a deficient imbalance in what sustains the body, hunger, thirst, and weakness. Because of no such deficiency or imbalance, strength and satiation. Because of a disordered, changing imbalance, sickness. Because of imbalance accumulating over time, ageing. Because of the vital faculty's own imbalance, death. Because of some disorder in the blood, itching. Because of improper food causing imbalance, fainting. Because earth and water combine, stickiness. Because of imbalance from constant coming and going, fatigue. Being free of this, through balance, rest. Because of freedom from grime and lassitude, vigour.
All of this, taken together, describes six states of the four elements: pure-or-impure, firm-or-not-firm, sluggish, combined, imbalanced, and balanced. These six may in turn be expanded into eight. Whether eight or six, they are entirely equivalent.

items.title: Section: Two Consciousnesses Know Every Object, and Why the Form Realm Has No Smell or Taste

items.zh: 復次，一切色乃至觸，皆二識所識，謂自識所識及意識所識。或漸、或頓。眼等五根，一意識所識。復次，色界中無現香、味，然有彼界。何以故？此二皆是叚食攝故。由無此二，鼻、舌二識亦無。此就現行說，非就界說。
items.en: Furthermore, all objects from colour through touch are known by two consciousnesses — one's own dedicated consciousness and mental consciousness — either gradually or suddenly. The five faculties of eye and the rest are known by mental consciousness alone. Furthermore, the form realm has no present smell or taste, though it still has their seeds. Why? Because both belong to solid food. Lacking these two, nose- and tongue-consciousness are also absent. This is spoken of present function, not of the seed.

items.title: Section: What Is Genuinely Real Within Form, and What Is Merely a Convenient Label

items.zh: 如是一切色蘊所攝。色中九種是實物有。觸所攝中，四大種是實物有。當知所餘唯是假有。
items.en: All of this is subsumed under form aggregate. Nine kinds of matter among these are genuinely real substances. Among what is subsumed under touch, the four elements are genuinely real substances. One should know that everything else is merely provisional.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Mind-Object Matter, From the Subtlest Particle to Form Born of Mastery in Meditation

items.zh: 墮法處色亦有二種，謂實有、假有。若有威德定所行境，猶如變化，彼果彼境及彼相應識等境色，是實物有。若律儀色、不律儀色，皆是假有。
items.en: Matter subsumed under the mental sense-field is also of two kinds: real and provisional. Whatever falls within the domain of one possessed of great meditative power, resembling a transformation, together with its result, its object, and the matter that serves as object for the consciousness and the rest associated with it, is genuinely real matter. Precept-vows, whether wholesome or unwholesome, are entirely provisional.

blocks.text: A close analysis of matter. Which parts of what we call "form" are real, and which are names for states of the elements?

subs.head: What form and mind depend on

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: the faculties depend on the supporting organ, the visible eye or ear, as distinct from the invisible pure-form faculty itself.

subs.head: How many things make an eye

blocks.text: One by characteristic, seven by inseparability, ten by element. Master Cháng Bǎi: by its own characteristic the eye is one thing, the pure-form faculty on which eye-consciousness relies.

Master Cháng Bǎi: sound is intermittent, appearing only when there are conditions, yet its element can be counted everywhere. (Untranslated, 0597a04: "its characteristic is the pure form on which body-consciousness relies.")
Master Cháng Bǎi: these are all phases of earth, water, fire, and wind, provisionally named. Sickness is a disorder of the elements; ageing, their imbalance over time.

All objects are known by their own consciousness and by mental consciousness. The form realm has no smell or taste in use, since both belong to solid food. Master Cháng Bǎi: those gods take the joy of meditation as food.
Nine kinds of matter are real (the five faculties and four sense objects other than touch), and within touch the four elements; the rest is provisional.

Form born of meditation is "its result and its object". Precept-vows, wholesome or unwholesome, are entirely provisional. Master Cháng Bǎi: they are set up on a phase of the seed of volition, arising from a strong resolve.
"Sickness is a disorder of the elements." The treatise is precise: sickness is real as experience, but it is not an extra substance in the body.

quiz.q: 相攝 is "by characteristic" in §21 and "according to essential nature" in §23. According to the lecture, how should this be viewed?
options: the Chinese differs in the two places, so separate renderings are right; they are not one term, and the two have nothing to do with each other
相攝 means mutual inclusion, so both are wrong and it should be "mutual subsumption"
one term has two renderings; the lecture says each aggregate has its own mark, and in §23 the eye is one thing, the pure form on which eye-consciousness relies
相攝 means outward resemblance, so both are wrong and it should be "similarity"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each aggregate has its own mark, form change and obstruction, feeling reception, and so on; and by the eye's own characteristic it is one thing, the pure-form faculty on which eye-consciousness relies. So one term is meant in both places, and the English should use one rendering. "Characteristic" is the more literal.

quiz.q: Among form's six grounds, what are the ground the faculties depend upon and the domain of powerful absorption?
options: the first is the pure-form faculty itself; the second a hallucination in absorption, without real function, merely appearing to exist
the first is the visible outer form of eye, ear, and so on; the second is form transformed in absorption, with real function
the first is the store-consciousness; the second is suchness
the first is the physical world; the second is the palaces of heaven
quiz.why: The treatise lists six grounds of form. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ground the faculties depend upon is the supporting organ, the visible outer form of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body, as distinct from the invisible pure-form faculty; and form transformed in absorption has real function, which is why it is counted as a ground.

quiz.q: Of the seven grounds of the four name-aggregates, how many does each kind of person rely on?
options: those enjoying pleasure one; those upholding discipline or diligent four; those with access concentration one; those in fundamental absorption one
all beings rely equally on the seven, with no difference, since the four name-aggregates function the same way everywhere
those enjoying pleasure four; those upholding discipline or diligent one; those with access concentration one; those in fundamental absorption one
those enjoying pleasure seven; other practitioners rely on none
quiz.why: The treatise assigns desire, hope, object, and investigation to those enjoying sensory pleasure; correct awareness to those upholding discipline or practising diligently; the means to purity to those with access concentration; and purity to those in fundamental absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi on correct awareness: at once knowing that mindfulness has lapsed is its work, and through it mindfulness is kept.

quiz.q: The English has "how many things does the eye ... subsume?" for 眼，幾物所攝. What is wrong with the voice?
options: the Chinese asks how many things the eye sees; "subsume" should be "see"
the Chinese asks how many owners possess the eye; the English omits the owners and the question of whose faculty it is
nothing is wrong: 攝 has no voice here, and the English is exact
the Chinese asks by how many things the eye is constituted; the English has the eye subsume things, reversing active and passive
quiz.why: The Chinese is passive, asking how many things go to make up the eye. Master Cháng Bǎi: in terms of the form inseparable from the eye faculty, there are seven kinds. The English "does the eye subsume" makes the eye the one that includes; the answers of one, seven, and ten only make sense as counts of what the eye consists of.

quiz.q: How many things does the eye have by characteristic, inseparability, and element?
options: one; ten, adding water, fire, and wind elements; seven, the eye with body, earth, colour, smell, taste, and touch
seven; one; ten, all reckoned by the same standard
one; seven, the eye with body, earth, colour, smell, taste, touch; ten, adding water, fire, and wind elements
one; five; eight, none including the body faculty
quiz.why: The treatise counts one thing by characteristic, seven by inseparability, and ten by element, adding the water, fire, and wind elements. For the body it excludes the eye and the other three. Master Cháng Bǎi: without eyes, ears, nose, or tongue, the body can still exist on its own; so the eye implies the body, but not the reverse.

quiz.q: The English has "the sound-element is present everywhere" after "not constantly present." What is the conflict, and how is it resolved?
options: the Chinese itself contradicts, an error of the treatise that the English faithfully keeps, needing no explanation
sound as a mark is intermittent; 界 is seed, and the sound-element may be added everywhere; the English drops 增 and seems to contradict itself
the sound-element is the ear faculty, which exists everywhere
the sound-element is space, which pervades everywhere
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: sound is intermittent, appearing only when there are conditions; but by subsumption of elements, one can add the sound-element to everything, eye through touch. So the Chinese distinguishes sound as manifest from sound as seed, and 增 says it is added to the count. The English drops "added" and sounds like a contradiction.

quiz.q: The English has "What is said of touch — smoothness up through vigour." What is missing, and why does it matter?
options: 造色 is missing: the point is that these derived tactile forms are only provisionally set on phases of the elements
中 is missing: the Chinese names a middle part of touch, and the English loses its place in the body
滑 is missing: the English fails to give "smoothness"
勇 is missing: the English fails to give "vigour"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these are all states of phases of earth, water, fire, and wind, provisionally designated. The treatise's subject is the derived form within touch: is it real? The English "What is said of touch" leaves out 造色, so a reader cannot see that the elements themselves remain real while the derived tactile qualities are provisional.

quiz.q: What within the form aggregate is substantially real?
options: all eleven kinds of form are real, with none provisional at all
only the four elements are real, all else including the five faculties being provisional, since it is derived from them
nine kinds of form, and the four elements within touch; all else merely provisional
only the five faculties are real, and outer objects provisional
quiz.why: The treatise says nine kinds of matter are real, and among what touch subsumes the four elements are real; the rest is merely provisional. Master Cháng Bǎi: the nine are eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and colour, sound, smell, and taste; the four elements are the producers, and these are real. Smoothness and the like are not.

quiz.q: Why are sickness, ageing, and death as tactile objects provisional? How does Master Cháng Bǎi sum up the twenty?
options: sickness, ageing, and death come from outer spirits, not from the body, and so are provisional
they describe the imbalance of the body's elements; all twenty are phases of the elements, and so provisional
all twenty are imagined by mind, unrelated to the elements, vanishing once one stops thinking of them
all twenty are real, "provisional" being a manner of speaking
quiz.why: The treatise derives sickness from disordered imbalance and ageing from imbalance over time. Master Cháng Bǎi: sickness describes a state of imbalance in the body's four elements, and so is provisionally established; the twenty tactile sensations all describe bodily feeling and are all differences in phase of the four elements, and so all are provisional.

quiz.q: "Gradually or suddenly" known by two consciousnesses: how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: one's own consciousness is the store-consciousness; gradual is slow awakening, sudden is immediate awakening
one's own consciousness is the five taking the five objects; gradual is one kind at a time, sudden is taking different kinds at once
one's own consciousness is mental consciousness; gradual is by day, sudden in dreams, both done by that one consciousness
one's own consciousness is manas; gradual has gaps and sudden has none
quiz.why: The treatise says all objects are known by one's own consciousness and by mental consciousness, gradually or suddenly. Master Cháng Bǎi: the five consciousnesses taking the five outer objects are "one's own consciousness"; sudden means taking objects of different kinds at the same time, and gradual means taking only one kind at a time. The topic is cognition, not awakening.

quiz.q: Does the form realm have smell and taste, and why?
options: manifest smell and taste exist, subtler than below; gods feed on them, and so nose- and tongue-consciousness remain
no manifest smell or taste, yet their elements remain; both belong to solid food, and so nose- and tongue-consciousness are absent
both manifest smell and taste and their elements are wholly gone, so they could not arise again
smell exists but not taste, since gods do not eat
quiz.why: The treatise says the form realm has no present smell or taste, though it has their elements, since both belong to solid food; this is spoken of function, not element. Master Cháng Bǎi: these gods take meditative joy as food, sustaining the body by absorption without eating; but as seeds, the seeds of smell and taste are still there.

quiz.q: The English has "together with ... the consciousness and mental factors corresponding to it, is genuinely real matter." What is the problem of attribution?
options: 彼果 is the result of karma, not of absorption, so "resulting object" misattributes it and should be corrected
識等境色 is form taken as object by the corresponding mind; the English reads as if consciousness and factors were themselves real matter
the Chinese says provisional, so "genuinely real" reverses it
the Chinese has no 識, which the English has added
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this real form subsumed under the mental sense-field is the result born of fundamental absorption and the domain in which it operates, and hence is called its result and its object. The phrase 識等境色 means form that is the object of the corresponding mind. The English syntax lists consciousness among what is "real matter," which cannot be intended.

quiz.q: Why are the form of vows, wholesome and unwholesome, provisional, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the vow is subtle real form derived from the elements, called provisional only because it cannot be seen
the vow is bestowed by the ordination platform and lapses away from it
the vow is the Buddha's blessing, not something in the recipient
the vow arises from strong resolve and time-limit, and is provisionally set on a phase of the seed of volition
quiz.why: The treatise says precept-vows, wholesome or unwholesome, are entirely provisional. Master Cháng Bǎi: this too is provisionally established, on a phase of the seed of volition; a vow arises because of a strong resolve and a set term, and so it is provisional, set up on volition. This agrees with the preceding fascicle's account of unexpressed karma.
